questions.question: Explain the shape of the water molecule using VSEPR theory.
questions.solution:
In H₂O, oxygen is sp³ hybridised with **two bond pairs and two lone pairs**.

According to VSEPR, lone pair–lone pair repulsion is greater than lone pair–bond pair repulsion, which compresses the tetrahedral angle from 109.5° to about **104.5°**.

Hence the shape of H₂O is **bent (angular or V-shaped)**.

questions.question: Define ionisation energy. Why does it increase across a period?
questions.solution:
**Ionisation energy** is the minimum energy required to remove the most loosely bound electron from an isolated gaseous atom.

Across a period nuclear charge increases while the shell number stays the same, so electrons are held more strongly — more energy is needed to remove them. Hence IE increases across a period.

questions.question: What are isotopes? Give one example.
questions.solution:
**Isotopes** are atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers (different numbers of neutrons).

Example: protium (¹₁H), deuterium (²₁H) and tritium (³₁H) — isotopes of hydrogen; also ¹²C and ¹⁴C.

questions.question: Write a short note on Graham's law of diffusion.
questions.solution:
**Graham's law:** at constant temperature and pressure, the rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass: r ∝ 1/√M, so r₁/r₂ = √(M₂/M₁).

Lighter gases diffuse faster — e.g. hydrogen diffuses about four times faster than oxygen.
